notes: §1985:VI.6.19.3 SR3: "When the CORRESPONDING phrase is used, all identifiers must be group items." CorrespondingBinder.Bind screens both operands of MOVE CORRESPONDING / CORR through CheckCorrespondingGroupOperand, which refuses with COBOL1757 an operand whose GroupKindsOf is none and a reference-modified operand, at every edition (no edition arm; the group kinds 2023 adds cannot be declared at 85). Probed at --std 85: an elementary sender, an elementary receiver, a level-77 item, a qualified elementary item, a level-66 alias of an elementary item and a reference-modified group are each refused; a subordinate group, a subscripted group and a qualified group are accepted. A level-66 RENAMES ... THRU alias is accepted as the group item it is; its refusal at 85 belongs to §1985:VI.6.4.3 rule (3) ("must not contain level-number 66, 77, or 88"), row 1985-GR-VI.6.4.3-3, kb/Work PB5105, not to this rule. The witness is an elementary receiver.

next.reason: 1985: "When the CORRESPONDING phrase is used, all identifiers must be group items."; 2023: "Identifier-3 and identifier-4 shall specify group data items and shall not be reference-modified.". Both require group items for MOVE CORRESPONDING. 2023 also forbids reference-modifying the operands, a refusal the 1985 rule text does not state.
